summary: The North Rim Restoration Act allows the National Park Service to use emergency contracting methods and noncompetitive procurement to restore areas of the Grand Canyon National Park impacted by the Dragon Bravo Fire, without requiring a presidential disaster declaration.

affected_groups.effect: Gains expedited emergency contracting and noncompetitive procurement powers to clear, rebuild, and maintain the fire-impacted areas of Grand Canyon National Park.
May be awarded noncompetitive procurement contracts if determined by the Secretary to be uniquely positioned to execute recovery work.

key_provisions: Allows the National Park Service to use emergency acquisition flexibilities for forest management, rebuilding structures, grounds improvements, and recovery efforts within areas impacted by the Dragon Bravo Fire without a presidential disaster declaration.

Grants authority to enter into noncompetitive (sole-source) procurement contracts for operating, repairing, or replacing assets like lodging, employee housing, and utility systems to support reopening the North Rim.
Requires the Secretary of the Interior to submit progress and expenditure reports every 180 days to specified congressional committees.
Authorizes the Secretary to request a 12-month extension of the emergency contracting authority if a new wildfire ignites in the area and disrupts recovery.
Sets an expiration date for the emergency contracting and noncompetitive procurement authorities at the earlier of seven years after enactment or when recovery projects are completed.
missing_information: Total estimated cost of the recovery efforts and funding sources.
Specific names of contractors or concessioners involved.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The North Rim Restoration Act allows the National Park Service to use emergency contracting methods and noncompetitive procurement to restore areas of the Grand Canyon National Park impacted by the Dragon Bravo Fire, without requiring a presidential disaster declaration.
summary_detail.significance: This bill modifies standard federal contracting laws specifically for Grand Canyon National Park to speed up post-wildfire recovery efforts over a period of up to seven years.
